data.updated: 20 September 2026 (evening — NO LEVEL, GEOGRAPHY OR REVISION-DATE CHANGE on any of the five markets. The evening tier-A sweep asserted complete (18 sources, exit 0). NEW AND DIARISED — CANADA’S EBOLA BORDER MEASURES EXPIRE 28 SEPTEMBER 2026 AT 23:59 EDT. Travel.gc.ca Travel Health Notice 549 (Level 3, avoid non-essential travel to DRC; original publication 15 May 2026, LAST MODIFIED 28 AUGUST 2026, read directly 20 September 2026) states the Government of Canada extended the existing temporary measures under the Quarantine Act “for another 30 days” and that they are “now in place until September 28, 2026 (23:59 EDT)”. Scope: Canadian citizens, permanent residents, persons registered under the Indian Act and foreign nationals who have been in the DRC, UGANDA or SOUTH SUDAN in the past 21 days. Foreign nationals who have been in the DRC in the past 21 days remain PROHIBITED from entering Canada or boarding a flight to Canada; those who have been in UGANDA or SOUTH SUDAN may travel but must QUARANTINE 21 DAYS on arrival unless exempt. READ THE STALENESS PRECISELY: that same Canadian notice still describes the outbreak as being in FOUR provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, Haut-Uléé and Tshopo — as rendered) against WHO’s six and the seven carried since Sud-Ubangi, and still states “related cases have been reported in neighbouring Uganda” — WHO certified Uganda outbreak-free on 26 AUGUST 2026, two days before the page was last modified. TWO WESTERN ENTRY REGIMES ON UGANDA NOW EXPIRE EIGHTEEN DAYS APART: Canada 28 September 2026 and the CDC Title 42 order (91 FR 58673–58679) 4:59pm EDT 11 October 2026. Logged as ledger call P198. ADVISORY LEVELS UNCHANGED. UK FCDO re-checked on all four: KENYA unchanged (against all travel to Mandera, parts of Wajir near the frontier, most of Garissa and mainland Lamu; page last updated late June 2026, marked current at 29 August 2026). UGANDA unchanged, last substantive update 2 September 2026 recording WHO’s 27 August declaration; the UK still advises against travel to NO part of Uganda. TANZANIA unchanged — all-but-essential within 20km of the Cabo Delgado border, Kigoma refugee camps, and heightened health screening for arrivals from Uganda and the DRC; Zanzibar unrestricted. RWANDA unchanged on the September revision (DRC-Ebola border measures and the vape/e-cigarette ban; all-but-essential to parts of Rusizi within 10km of the DRC border; Gisenyi–Goma may close at short notice). CANADA unchanged on Kenya, last updated 9 September 2026, “exercise a high degree of caution” with avoid-all-travel for Mandera, Wajir, Garissa and Lamu. GERMANY unchanged (July 2026 revision). FRANCE unchanged — the 100km Somalia-border exclusion stands, and note its standing OCTOBER–DECEMBER clause warning of El Niño-accentuated short rains, flash flooding, landslides on road axes including in urban areas, and a resurgence of cholera, typhoid and malaria. RWANDA ENTRY RULE unchanged: the Rwanda MoH notice of 22 May 2026 denying entry to foreign nationals who travelled to or transited the DRC in the previous 30 days is unrevised, with thermal imaging and screening at Gisenyi and other DRC/Uganda crossings. ZANZIBAR: Travel Advisory No. 1 of 20 May 2026 remains the operative notice — universal non-invasive temperature screening at all air and sea points of entry and a Traveller Surveillance Form for arrivals from or transiting affected areas; Tanzania still records zero Ebola cases. HEALTH — DRC UPDATED: WHO now carries 7,475 CONFIRMED CASES AND 3,605 DEATHS to 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 across 61 health zones (up from the 7,404 and 3,577 to 15 September we carried last night), with 2,007 people vaccinated across six health zones in three provinces to 6 September. Africa CDC said on 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 that the outbreak is “still serious”, with data showing gaps in infection prevention and control, and its Emergency Consultative Group issued recommendations on persistent community deaths and contact-identification gaps. Bundibugyo species; no licensed vaccine or specific treatment. UGANDA: no new cases since 21 June 2026; 28 July declaration and 26 August WHO certification stand, final toll 20 confirmed cases and 2 deaths. BLIND SPOTS DECLARED: Africa CDC’s latest posted Epidemic Intelligence Weekly remains the AUGUST 2026 edition and tonight’s Africa CDC read is from reporting of its 17 September briefing, not the bulletin. Zanzibar’s Ministry of Health was again not read directly. The Kenya Gazette mirrors returned empty bodies and were recovered via Kenya Law direct-source URLs and press.)

us.note: Terrorism, crime, kidnapping, unrest, health and 'Other'. Country level unchanged at 2. Re-issued 28 July 2026 (rendered page carries 'Date issued: July 28, 2026', verified 12 Aug 2026) — the 'Other (O)' indicator was added and the Nairobi neighbourhoods of EASTLEIGH and KIBERA are now LEVEL 4 DO NOT TRAVEL (crime, kidnapping), corrected from our earlier Level 3 reading. Also Level 4: Garissa, Wajir, Mandera, Lamu, Tana River (except Tsavo NP), Kilifi north of the C103 and coastal areas north of Malindi; West Pokot and western Turkana; Marsabit and Turkana within 50km of Ethiopia. Nairobi hotel corridors (Westlands, Upper Hill, Gigiri, CBD, Karen), Diani and Watamu are not in any Level 4 area.

uk.note: Against travel to the Kenya–Somalia border and parts of Lamu/north coast; core safari & coast areas unaffected. HEALTH LAYER (separate from the advisory): three G7 governments now carry a dengue notice on Kenya naming the COAST — US Embassy Nairobi health alert 3 Aug 2026 (coast, Wajir, Garissa); Germany 3 Aug 2026; CANADA added Kenya to Travel Health Notice 517 on 8 Sep 2026. Canada’s notice is Level 1 — practise health precautions — and did NOT change any country risk level. Kenya MoH: 1,678 dengue cases and 5 suspected deaths in Garissa and Wajir as at 26 Aug 2026 (1,276 in Dadaab), PHEOC activated; separately Mombasa recorded 3,989 cases Jan–May 2026 (Health CS Aden Duale via The Standard). The UK has NOT added a dengue line to its Kenya health page as at 9 Sep 2026.

us.note: Do not travel — VERIFIED against travel.state.gov 3 Sep 2026. Date issued 4 June 2026; indicators Crime, Health, Terrorism, Unrest. Advisory history states Uganda was raised from Level 3 to Level 4 on 17 May 2026 'due to the Ebola Bundibugyo Virus Disease outbreak in Ituri Province in the DRC'. The page still describes Kampala mass-gathering restrictions, 21-day quarantine for DRC arrivals and the DRC border closure. NOT UPDATED since 4 June — 91 days — despite Uganda MoH declaring the outbreak over on 28 Jul 2026 and WHO certifying the end on 26 Aug 2026. State's own text links to a CDC travel health notice filed under a Level 2 path. Divergence with the UK (Level 1) is now two full levels.

uk.note: CORRECTED 28 Aug 2026 — the UK advises against travel to NO part of Uganda. We carried 'against all-but-essential travel to Queen Elizabeth & Semuliki NP' for nine months after the FCDO lifted it on 2 December 2025. Verified against gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/uganda and its Regional risks page, 28 Aug 2026: still current at 25 Aug 2026, updated 27 Jul 2026, and the Warnings page carries no advice-against-travel block at all. Every 'advises against all travel' line on the Regional risks page refers to the DRC and South Sudan, NOT Uganda. Western Uganda carries caution language only (ADF, Kasese/Bundibugyo attacks Nov 2025). Bwindi and Mgahinga are open; armed escort on gorilla tracking is described as routine practice, not a warning. NOTE: mandatory National Cleaning Day, final Saturday monthly 07:00-10:00, nationwide movement restriction — tourists exempt (Uganda Police, 24 Aug 2026).

us.note: Reconsider travel — RAISED from Level 2 to 3 on 31 Oct 2025 ('unrest' indicator added). Grounds: unrest, crime, terrorism (highest risk in the Mtwara Region near the Mozambique border), and targeting of gay & lesbian individuals. Verified vs travel.state.gov 4 Aug 2026.

uk.note: No advisory against travel except within 20km of the Mozambique (Cabo Delgado) border.

us.note: As mainland Tanzania (Level 3 since 31 Oct 2025); no Zanzibar-specific carve-out. Verified 4 Aug 2026.
Reconsider travel — regional Ebola risk and DRC border security.

uk.note: CORRECTED 8 Sep 2026 — the FCDO advice-against area is PARTS OF RUSIZI DISTRICT ONLY: the parts within 10km of the DRC border, including the Rwandan islands in Lake Kivu and Kamembe Airport. RUBAVU IS NOT NAMED. We carried 'Rubavu, Rusizi' and were overstating it — Gisenyi/Rubavu on Lake Kivu carries no advice against travel, and Kigali, Musanze/Volcanoes, Nyungwe and Akagera are all outside the advice-against area. Verified by reading gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/rwanda/entry-requirements directly on 8 Sep 2026; the page's own public-updated-at is 4 Sep 2026 10:15 BST. ENTRY RULE, separate from the advisory: Rwanda denies entry to any foreign national who has travelled to or transited through the DRC in the 30 days before travel, and runs enhanced screening at Kigali International Airport and DRC land crossings (Rwanda MoH notice, 22 May 2026; FCDO links to RBC for it). Commonwealth citizens get a free 30-day visa on arrival.
